model.name: Quantity / Unit
model.purpose: Governed embeddable context for a quantity value as a number with a reference unit, plus the quantity kind, dimension, scale type, coded unit, conversion semantics and measurement uncertainty needed to create, inspect, convert and operate quantities without binding the mixin to a storage format.
model.scope_statement: This mixin covers the metrological and computational meaning of quantities and units: quantity kinds and dimensions in a system of quantities; units, prefixes and systems of units; the quantity-value tuple of numerical value and unit; scale type and permissible algebra; coded unit vocabularies; conversion and dimensional homogeneity; and the GUM expression of uncertainty attached to a quantity value. It is an embeddable value-object mixin, not a standalone measured-object, instrument, currency, calendar or geometry model.
in_scope: Quantity kinds, including base and derived kinds of the International System of Quantities, and the distinction between a kind and a particular quantity of that kind.
Quantity dimension as a product of powers of base dimensions, including quantities of dimension one.
Units of measurement: names, symbols, identities, base versus derived versus coherent units, and membership of a system of units.
SI defining constants and the seven SI base units as the governing alignment for physical units.
Decimal SI prefixes and, as an alignment not a claim of SI membership, IEC binary prefixes used with information units.
Quantity value as numerical value times unit, including implicit precision, significant digits and style conventions for printing values.
Coded unit expressions and tabulated unit codes for machine interchange, including UCUM, UN/ECE Recommendation 20 and QUDT IRIs.
Commensurability, semantic equality of unit expressions, conversion multipliers and offsets, and quantity calculus under dimensional homogeneity.
Special units on interval or logarithmic scales, counting units, dimensionless ratios, and procedure-defined arbitrary units that are not convertible.
Delta versus absolute quantities, especially temperature interval versus thermodynamic temperature.
Censored or inequality-qualified values, inclusive ranges and ratios of quantities.
Measurement uncertainty attached to a quantity value: standard, combined and expanded uncertainty, coverage factor and coverage probability.
Metrological traceability of a unit or conversion factor to an international reference, and mapping among unit vocabularies.
Provenance, versioning, deprecation, allowed-unit policy, original-versus-converted value retention, and the AGENTS.md bootstrap contract for this mixin.
out_of_scope: Currency and money as economic instruments identified by ISO 4217; QUDT CurrencyUnit and FHIR Money are alignments only, not in-scope quantity kinds.
Calendar instants, time zones, leap-second civil time and ISO 8601 date-time identity; duration as a quantity of time remains in scope, the time-point does not.
Spatial geometry, coordinate reference systems, geodetic datums and pixel or device-dependent presentation units.
The measured object, sensor, instrument, laboratory, observer, sampling protocol and full measurement event; those belong to a host Observation or Measurement model that this mixin embeds into.
Unit of presentation such as tablet, vial or puff as defined for medicinal-product packaging, distinct from unit of measurement.
Legal metrology enforcement, type approval, market surveillance and OIML certificate lifecycle as a legal process model.
Statistical method design beyond the GUM expression of an already-evaluated uncertainty, and full digital calibration-certificate document models.
Vector, tensor, complex or phasor quantities as first-class types; only a scalar magnitude plus optional uncertainty is modelled here unless a host model supplies the remainder.
Nominal classifications that are not quantities, including coded categories that only happen to use numeric labels.

boundary_notes.distinction: This mixin supplies the value, unit, kind, dimension and uncertainty of a result. The host model owns who measured what, with which instrument, under which procedure, at which place and time. A quantity value is not itself a measurement event.

Monetary amounts use ISO 4217 currency codes and accounting precision rules. They are not SI quantities, are not dimensionally convertible to physical units, and FHIR separates Money from Quantity. This mixin may record that a coded unit is a currency only as an out-of-scope exclusion flag.

A duration (second, hour, day as a unit of time) is a quantity. A timestamp with offset is an instant identity, not a quantity. UCUM and SI treat day, hour and minute as units of duration; they are not calendar dates.

Length, area, volume and plane angle are quantities. Positions, CRS identifiers, geoids and pixel grids are spatial identities. Plane angle is dimensionless in the SI but treated as a distinct dimension in UCUM, which is an alignment conflict, not a reason to absorb geometry.

ISO 11240 governs units of measurement for strength and composition. Units of presentation (tablet, ampoule) describe how a product is counted or administered, not a metrological unit, and must not be stored as UCUM atoms without an annotation or a sibling model.

A unit code is an identifier of a unit concept, not of the quantity value instance. Quantity values as embeddable value objects do not require their own master identifier unless a Dimension assigns a UUID for audit of a frozen original value.

sources.organization: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (JCGM) / BIPM

sources.title: The Unified Code for Units of Measure
sources.organization: Regenstrief Institute, Inc. and the UCUM Organization
sources.relevance: Machine-to-machine grammar and semantics for unit expressions, including equality, commensurability, special units, arbitrary units, prefixes and a non-SI base that is not isomorphic with the SI.

sources.relevance: Conceptual split of Quantity, QuantityKind, QuantityValue and Unit; dimension vectors; conversion multiplier and offset; delta quantities; scale types; and crosswalk properties for UCUM, UNECE and IEC 61360 codes.

sources.title: ISO 80000-1:2022 Quantities and units — Part 1: General
sources.relevance: General rules for the International System of Quantities, quantity and unit symbols, coherent unit systems, quantity calculus and the statement that a quantity is a product of a numerical value and a unit.
