bundles.name: Quantity kind and dimension
bundles.description: The conceptual layer that distinguishes a particular quantity from its kind, places that kind in a system of quantities, assigns a dimension vector, and records the measurement scale that governs permitted algebra.
bundles.rationale: VIM, ISO 80000-1 and QUDT all treat quantity kind and dimension as independent of any one numerical value or unit. Agents cannot convert, compare or validate a quantity until kind, dimension and scale type are known.

layers.name: Quantity versus quantity kind
layers.description: Definitions that separate an observable property of a particular object or event from the kind of that property, independent of any chosen unit.

findings.name: Quantity as a property with magnitude
findings.description: VIM defines a quantity as a property of a phenomenon, body or substance that can be expressed as a number and a reference. QUDT restates a quantity as the measurement of an observable property of a particular object, event or physical system, always in a measurement context, whereas the underlying quantity kind is independent of that measurement. ISO 80000-1 treats a quantity as the product of a numerical value and a unit. This mixin records that conceptual triple, not the host object.

questions.text: What quantity is being expressed, as a property of which phenomenon, body, substance, object or event, and is it a particular quantity or only a kind?
If this quantity instance must be cited independently of its host record, what master identifier, governed IRI or Dimension-assigned UUID identifies it?
Which host entity, observation or event embeds this quantity, and is the quantity a measured result, a specified requirement, a constant or a derived calculated value?
Is the quantity treated as a real scalar magnitude, or does the host need vector, tensor or complex structure that this mixin cannot carry alone?

data_elements.name: Quantity label
data_elements.description: Human-readable name of the particular quantity, such as rocket height or patient body mass, distinct from the quantity kind.

data_elements.name: Is particular quantity
data_elements.description: True when the record is a quantity of a specific object or event rather than only a quantity kind.

data_elements.name: Quantity role
data_elements.description: Whether the value is a measured result, specified limit, reference constant, counted amount or calculated derived value.

data_elements.name: Quantity instance identifier
data_elements.description: Optional identifier for a frozen original quantity value when the Dimension requires citation independent of the host. A date is not an identifier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The quantity concept is reference data carried on the host record. No separate artefact is required unless a Dimension freezes an original value as an auditable object.

findings.name: Quantity kind classification
findings.description: A quantity kind is any observable property that can be quantified, such as length, mass, time, force or information capacity. Kinds are related by physical laws so that some kinds are derived from others. The same dimension can host different kinds, for example energy versus torque or absorbed dose versus dose equivalent, so kind cannot be inferred from dimension alone.

questions.text: Which quantity kind applies, identified by ISQ name, QUDT QuantityKind IRI, or another governed kind code?
Is this kind a base quantity kind of the governing system of quantities, or a derived kind defined by an equation among kinds?
If other kinds share this dimension, what distinguishes this kind so that conversion or comparison with those kinds is refused?
Which units are applicable to this kind, and which system of units supplies the preferred unit?

data_elements.name: Quantity kind IRI
data_elements.description: Governed IRI of the quantity kind, preferably a QUDT QuantityKind or an ISQ-aligned identifier.

data_elements.name: Quantity kind code
data_elements.description: Code or name of the kind in the chosen kind system, such as length or absorbed dose.

data_elements.name: Is base quantity kind
data_elements.description: True when the kind is a base kind of the selected system of quantities.

data_elements.name: Same-dimension peer kinds
data_elements.description: Other quantity kinds that share the dimension vector but must not be treated as interchangeable.

artifacts.name: Quantity kind vocabulary extract
artifacts.description: Governed extract of allowed quantity kinds for the adopting Dimension, with IRIs, labels, dimensions and applicable units.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the vocabulary graph IRI and release version as the master identity; each kind uses its QUDT or Dimension IRI.

layers.name: Dimension and system of quantities
layers.description: Dimensional analysis context: exponents of base quantities and the system of quantities that defines those bases.

findings.name: Quantity dimension vector
findings.description: The dimension of a quantity is expressed as a product of powers of the base quantities of a system. In the SI the bases are length L, mass M, time T, electric current I, thermodynamic temperature Θ, amount of substance N and luminous intensity J. Two quantities of the same dimension are commensurable as units but not necessarily of the same kind. Implementations may bound exponent ranges; UCUM notes that practical exponents often lie between -4 and +4.

questions.text: What is the dimension vector of this quantity kind in the governing system, including exponents for L, M, T, I, Θ, N and J and any extra base such as angle?
Is this a quantity of dimension one, and if so is an explicit unit still required by SI guidance rather than leaving the unit blank?
Which system of dimensions is the vector expressed in, and is a mapping required because UCUM uses gram, radian and coulomb bases that are not isomorphic with the SI?
Against which other quantities must dimensional homogeneity be proven before addition, subtraction or equality comparison?

data_elements.name: Dimension vector IRI
data_elements.description: Identifier of a QUDT QuantityKindDimensionVector or equivalent SI dimension product.

data_elements.name: Is dimension one
data_elements.description: True when all base-dimension exponents are zero.

data_elements.name: Length exponent
data_elements.description: Rational or integer exponent of length in the dimension product.

data_elements.name: Dimension system
data_elements.description: Code for the dimension basis: SI, UCUM, CGS, Imperial or other.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A dimension vector is structured reference data on the quantity kind. It is stored inline or by IRI into a vocabulary, not as a standalone document.

findings.name: System of quantities
findings.description: A system of quantity kinds is a set of kinds plus the equations that relate them, typically identifying a base subset from which others are derived. The SI is coupled to the International System of Quantities. Choice of base kinds is conventional. A unit system associated with a quantity-kind system must define at least one unit for each kind of interest.

questions.text: Which system of quantities governs this record, and which base quantity kinds does that system declare?
Which defining equations or physical relations of the system are needed to derive this kind from the bases?
Which system of units is explicitly coupled to this system of quantities, and does it define a unit for every kind in use?

data_elements.name: System of quantities IRI
data_elements.description: Identifier of the governing system of quantity kinds, typically ISQ/SI.

data_elements.name: Base quantity kinds
data_elements.description: The base kinds declared by the system.

data_elements.name: Governing standard
data_elements.description: Citation of ISO 80000, the SI Brochure or another system definition.

artifacts.name: System of quantities register
artifacts.description: Dimension-governed register of the adopted system of quantities, its bases, equations and coupled unit system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master identity is the system IRI plus release version.

layers.name: Measurement scale type
layers.description: Scale of measurement that determines which algebraic operations and conversions are meaningful.

findings.name: Scale type and permissible mathematics
findings.description: QUDT distinguishes ratio, interval, ordinal, nominal, enumeration and logarithmic scales. Ratio scales have a non-arbitrary zero and support multiplication. Interval scales such as Celsius support differences but not true ratios. UCUM models non-ratio symbols as special units with forward and inverse functions rather than as members of the multiplicative group of proper units. Nominal labels are not quantities.

questions.text: What scale type applies to this quantity kind and unit pairing: ratio, interval, logarithmic, ordinal, enumeration or nominal?
Which operations are permitted on values of this scale: addition, subtraction, multiplication by a scalar, ratio, logarithm, or only order comparison?
If the unit is special, what forward and inverse functions convert between the special unit and its corresponding proper unit, including any scale factor from a prefix?

data_elements.name: Scale type
data_elements.description: Code for ratio, interval, logarithmic, ordinal, enumeration or nominal scale.

data_elements.name: Zero is absolute
data_elements.description: True when the scale has a unique non-arbitrary zero, as required for ratio statements such as twice as long.

data_elements.name: Special unit conversion function
data_elements.description: Named function mapping a proper-unit magnitude to the special-unit numerical value, for example Celsius from kelvin.

data_elements.name: Allows multiplication
data_elements.description: True when multiplication of the unit by a scalar is defined so that SI prefixes are metrically meaningful.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scale type and permitted operations are classification metadata on kind and unit. They are inline reference data.

bundles.name: Unit of measurement
bundles.description: Identity, classification, prefixes, systems of units, and the special, arbitrary and counting units that sit outside ordinary ratio-scale algebra.
bundles.rationale: A quantity value is meaningless without a unit. Agents must know whether a unit is SI-coherent, prefixed, customary, special, arbitrary or a trade code, and which authority defines it.

layers.name: Unit identity and classification
layers.description: How a unit is named, symbolised, identified and classed as base, derived, coherent, allowed or non-SI.

findings.name: Unit identifiers and symbols
findings.description: A unit is a particular quantity value chosen as a scale for other quantities of the same kind. Identity priority is an authoritative master identifier such as a QUDT unit IRI or SI Brochure definition, then a governed global code such as a case-sensitive UCUM atom or UNECE common code, then a UUID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Print names and typographic symbols are defined by BIPM and ISO 80000 and are out of scope of UCUM; UCUM normative columns are the case-sensitive code, case-insensitive code, metric predicate, magnitude and definitional expression.

questions.text: What is the authoritative master identifier of this unit, and which additional coded identities (UCUM case-sensitive, UCUM case-insensitive, UNECE Rec 20, IEC 61360, QUDT IRI) are bound to it?
What print name and print symbol should humans see, and is that display form allowed to differ from the machine code without changing meaning?
Is the unit atom metric, so that an SI or UCUM prefix may attach, and is the atom itself prefix-free?
Which organisation and which version of which specification currently defines this unit, and has the definition been deprecated or replaced?

data_elements.name: Unit master identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the unit in the governing register.

data_elements.name: UCUM case-sensitive code
data_elements.description: Case-sensitive UCUM expression or atom.

data_elements.name: UNECE Rec 20 common code
data_elements.description: Three-character UN/ECE Recommendation 20 code when used in trade messages.

data_elements.name: Print symbol
data_elements.description: Typographic symbol recommended for human display by BIPM or ISO 80000, not necessarily ASCII.

data_elements.name: Is metric unit atom
data_elements.description: UCUM metric predicate: only metric atoms may take prefixes.

artifacts.name: Unit register entry
artifacts.description: Serialised register record for one unit, including identifiers, symbols, metric predicate and definitional expression.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master identity is the unit IRI or code in the named register version; Dimension UUID only if no master IRI exists.

findings.name: Base, derived and coherent units
findings.description: The SI retains seven historically chosen base units even though the system is now defined by seven constants. Derived units are products of powers of base units. A coherent derived unit has a proportionality factor of one. UCUM replaces kilogram with gram as a syntactic base and uses radian and coulomb in its defining basis, so UCUM is not isomorphic with the SI. Coherence is always relative to a named system.

questions.text: In the named system of units, is this unit a base unit, a coherent derived unit, a non-coherent derived unit, or merely allowed for use?
If this is an SI base unit, which defining constant and exact numerical value fix it after 20 May 2019?
What is the definitional expression of this unit as a product of powers of the system's base units, including any numeric factor?

data_elements.name: Unit class in system
data_elements.description: base, derived-coherent, derived-non-coherent, allowed-non-si, or customary.

data_elements.name: Is coherent
data_elements.description: True when the unit is a product of powers of the system's base units with factor one.

data_elements.name: Definitional unit expression
data_elements.description: Algebraic expression in the governing grammar that defines the unit, for example N = kg.m/s2.

data_elements.name: Defining constant
data_elements.description: Name of the SI defining constant when the unit is an SI base unit, such as Planck constant h.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification relative to a system of units is reference metadata on the unit record.

layers.name: Prefixes and multiples
layers.description: Decimal and binary prefixes that scale metric unit atoms, and the SI prefix set including later additions.

findings.name: Decimal and binary prefixes
findings.description: SI decimal prefixes multiply a metric unit atom by a power of ten. UCUM Table 1 lists yotta through yocto with case-sensitive and case-insensitive codes; prefix parsing takes the longest leading match. QUDT separately models BinaryPrefix for powers of two used with information units. The 27th CGPM added ronna, quetta, ronto and quecto; the UCUM 2.2 prefix table fetched on this research pass still ends at yotta/yocto, which is a live alignment gap. Prefixes on special units scale the numerical value through a scale factor rather than multiplying a ratio-scale unit.

questions.text: Which prefix, if any, is applied, what is its exact scalar value, and is it a decimal SI prefix or a binary information prefix?
Is prefixing legal on this atom, and has a double prefix or a prefix on a non-metric atom been rejected?
Which prefix set version is in force, and does it include ronna, quetta, ronto and quecto or only the UCUM 2.2 yotta-to-yocto set?
If the unit is an information unit, must IEC binary prefixes be used instead of SI decimal prefixes to avoid kilo versus kibi ambiguity?

data_elements.name: Prefix symbol
data_elements.description: Case-sensitive prefix symbol such as k, M, u, or Ki.

data_elements.name: Prefix scalar
data_elements.description: Exact power-of-ten or power-of-two multiplier.

data_elements.name: Prefix kind
data_elements.description: decimal or binary.

data_elements.name: Includes 2022 SI prefixes
data_elements.description: Whether the adopted prefix table includes ronna, quetta, ronto and quecto.

artifacts.name: Prefix table
artifacts.description: Governed table of prefix symbols, names, scalars and kind, versioned against SI Brochure and UCUM.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identity is specification URI plus table version date.

layers.name: Special, arbitrary and counting units
layers.description: Units that are not proper members of the multiplicative group, plus counts and logarithmic units.

findings.name: Special units on non-ratio scales
findings.description: UCUM defines special units as triples of a corresponding proper unit plus mutually inverse functions, because symbols such as degree Celsius, bel and neper are not elements of the Abelian group of proper units. They may be scaled by a prefix factor even though they are theoretically non-metric. Celsius remains in the SI despite being incoherent with kelvin; conversion is t/°C = T/K - 273.15. Temperature intervals may be expressed in kelvin or degree Celsius with the same magnitude.

questions.text: Is this unit a special non-ratio unit, and what corresponding proper unit and conversion functions apply?
Is the recorded value a level on the special scale, or a difference/interval that must use offset-free conversion?
If a prefix is attached to a special unit, what scale factor divides the function output so that milli-degree Celsius is not treated as 0.001 times a Celsius temperature?

data_elements.name: Is special unit
data_elements.description: True when the unit is a UCUM special unit on a non-ratio scale.

data_elements.name: Corresponding proper unit
data_elements.description: The proper unit in the ratio-scale group, for example kelvin for degree Celsius.

data_elements.name: Is delta quantity
data_elements.description: True when the value is an interval or change and conversion must not apply an affine offset.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Special-unit semantics are definitional metadata and conversion functions, stored as reference data on the unit.

findings.name: Arbitrary, counting and logarithmic units
findings.description: Arbitrary units have meaning only for a named measurement procedure and are not commensurable with any other unit, including other arbitrary units. Counting units express counts, percents and rates of count. Logarithmic units such as the bit, bel and decibel express quantities defined on a logarithmic scale. UCUM annotations in curly braces do not change semantics and are equivalent to unity when they stand alone. FHIR Quantity also allows amounts involving arbitrary units.

questions.text: If the unit is arbitrary or procedure-defined, which assay, reference material or procedure defines it, and is conversion to any other unit forbidden?
If the value is a count, what is being counted, and is a UCUM annotation or a dimensionless unit one being used as a non-semantic label?
If the unit is logarithmic, what is the reference quantity and logarithmic base, and is the value a ratio of two quantities of the same kind?

data_elements.name: Is arbitrary unit
data_elements.description: True when the unit has no relation to SI units and cannot be compared with any other unit.

data_elements.name: Defining procedure identifier
data_elements.description: Reference to the assay or procedure that gives the arbitrary unit its meaning.

data_elements.name: UCUM annotation
data_elements.description: Curly-brace annotation that must be discarded for semantic comparison.

data_elements.name: Is counting unit
data_elements.description: True when the unit expresses a count or a count-derived rate rather than a continuous physical magnitude.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Arbitrary and counting semantics are flags and references on the unit or value, not independent documents.

layers.name: Systems of units
layers.description: Named systems that group base, derived and allowed units, including SI, customary, CGS and trade usage.

findings.name: Unit system membership
findings.description: A system of units chooses reference scales for a set of quantity kinds and defines each unit experimentally or by proportion. QUDT records whether a unit is a base, defined, coherent, derived or merely allowed unit of a system. The SI Brochure lists units accepted for use with the SI, such as litre, tonne, day, electronvolt and astronomical unit, without making them SI units. Version 4.01 of the 9th edition clarifies the status of non-SI units. US customary, Imperial and CGS systems remain in practical use and must be named when conversion is performed.

questions.text: Which system or systems of units is this unit a member of, and in each system is it base, defined, coherent, derived or only allowed?
If the unit is outside the SI, is it accepted for use with the SI, tolerated in a named domain, or disallowed by Dimension policy?
If the unit is customary, which national or sectoral variant applies, such as US gallon versus Imperial gallon or avoirdupois versus troy mass?

data_elements.name: System of units IRI
data_elements.description: Identifier of the system of units, for example SI.

data_elements.name: SI acceptance status
data_elements.description: si-unit, accepted-for-use-with-si, other-non-si, or disallowed.

data_elements.name: Customary family
data_elements.description: Family such as US-customary, Imperial, apothecaries or troy when disambiguation is required.

artifacts.name: System of units register
artifacts.description: Register of adopted systems, their base units, allowed non-SI units and Dimension policy overlays.
artifacts.identity_strategy: System IRI plus brochure or vocabulary version.

bundles.name: Quantity value expression
bundles.description: How a magnitude is written as a numerical value with a bound unit, including precision, comparators, ranges, ratios and dimensionless expressions.
bundles.rationale: ISO 80000, NIST SP 811 and FHIR all operationalise Q = n × U. Interchange fails when precision, coded unit, human unit or inequality semantics are dropped.

layers.name: Numerical value and unit binding
layers.description: The core value object: number, implicit precision, human unit, coded unit and coding system.

findings.name: Numerical value and precision
findings.description: The numerical value of a quantity in a stated unit includes implicit precision in its presentation. FHIR decimal preserves trailing zeros so that 0.010 differs from 0.01 for presentation, while calculation engines may still use arbitrary precision. NIST SP 811 gives rounding rules for converted values. Monetary precision is out of scope. Exact SI defining-constant numerical values must not be rounded as if they were measured.

questions.text: What numerical value is recorded in the stated unit, and what precision or significant-digit count is implied by its lexical representation?
Was this number rounded, and if it was produced by conversion, what rounding rule from NIST SP 811 or Dimension policy was applied?
At what event time was the quantity true of the world, and at what observation or ingestion time was this numerical value recorded?

data_elements.name: Numerical value
data_elements.description: The number n in Q = n × U, preserving lexical precision where required.

data_elements.name: Lexical decimal
data_elements.description: Exact lexical representation of the decimal so that trailing zeros remain significant.

data_elements.name: Significant digits
data_elements.description: Count of significant digits when not implied solely by the lexical form.

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and explicit offset when the quantity described the world.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A numerical value is inline on the quantity value object. Rounding policy may be cited by reference rather than stored as a document.

findings.name: Unit binding on a quantity value
findings.description: FHIR Quantity binds an optional human-readable unit string, a coding system URI and a computer-processable code, with invariant qty-3 requiring a system whenever a code is present. UCUM is the preferred system for physical quantities; SNOMED CT may be used for some customary units; ISO 4217 is for currency and must not be mixed into this mixin. A UCUM code enables generation of a canonical value for comparison. ISO 11240 requires coded units for medicinal-product interchange and traceability to metrological standards.

questions.text: What coded unit, coding system URI and human-readable unit are bound to this value, and do they satisfy the rule that a code requires a system?
If a coded unit is missing, is the value unusable for conversion, and is a free-text unit or a dimensionless default of one being used?
Which unit coding system is required in this context of use, and is a translation from a local or trade code still pending?

data_elements.name: Unit code
data_elements.description: Computer-processable unit symbol or expression in the identified system.

data_elements.name: Unit coding system URI
data_elements.description: URI of the code system, for example http://unitsofmeasure.org for UCUM.

data_elements.name: Human-readable unit
data_elements.description: Display form of the unit, which may use micrograms as mcg or other local spellings.

data_elements.name: Required unit system
data_elements.description: Policy-required coding system for the context of use.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit binding is part of the quantity value object. Vocabulary resources are cited by URI rather than copied.

layers.name: Comparators, ranges and ratios
layers.description: Structures for inequality-qualified values, inclusive limits and ratios of two quantities.

findings.name: Comparator and censored values
findings.description: FHIR Quantity.comparator records that the true value is less than, less or equal, greater than, or greater or equal to the stated number because of measurement limits. Absence of a comparator means the number is unmodified. Sampled series additionally use sentinels for below and above detection limits. These flags change comparison and aggregation semantics and are therefore modifiers.

questions.text: Is the stated numerical value exact, or is it an inequality relative to a detection or reporting limit, and which comparator applies?
How must comparison, sorting and statistical aggregation treat this censored value so that it is not processed as an exact point?
Which instrument, method or laboratory defined the detection or quantitation limit that produced this comparator?

data_elements.name: Comparator
data_elements.description: One of <, <=, >=, > or absent meaning unmodified.

data_elements.name: Is censored
data_elements.description: True when the value is limited by detection or reporting limits rather than being a point estimate.

data_elements.name: Detection limit
data_elements.description: Numerical detection or quantitation limit in the same unit as the value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Comparator state is inline on the quantity value. Method references point to a host measurement model.

findings.name: Range and ratio structures
findings.description: A Range is an ordered pair of inclusive SimpleQuantity limits that must share commensurable units, with low less than or equal to high. A Ratio is two Quantity values used only when the relationship cannot be a single quantity with a compound unit; if the denominator is fixed at one, Quantity should be used instead. Both structures inherit unit-binding and comparator rules on each limb.

questions.text: If the quantity is a range, what are the inclusive low and high limits, in which units, and are the limits commensurable and ordered?
If the quantity is a ratio, what are the numerator and denominator quantities, and why can they not be expressed as a single compound unit?
Is either bound missing, meaning unknown rather than infinite, and how should membership tests treat an open bound?

data_elements.name: Range low
data_elements.description: Inclusive lower SimpleQuantity.

data_elements.name: Range high
data_elements.description: Inclusive upper SimpleQuantity.

data_elements.name: Ratio numerator
data_elements.description: Numerator quantity of a ratio.

data_elements.name: Ratio denominator
data_elements.description: Denominator quantity of a ratio.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Range and ratio are inline structured values composed of quantity limbs.

layers.name: Dimensionless quantities and unit one
layers.description: Quantities of dimension one, the unit one, angles, and SI guidance to use explicit units.

findings.name: Dimensionless quantities and the unit one
findings.description: Quantities of dimension one historically used an omitted unit or the unit one. SI Brochure version 3.01 strengthened guidance that explicit units should be employed wherever possible for such quantities, and version 4.01 further clarified non-SI units and related wording. UCUM treats the number one as unity, provides percent and parts-per-N atoms, and deprecates ppb and pptr because billion and trillion are internationally ambiguous. Plane angle is dimensionless in the SI with the radian as a derived unit of dimension one, but UCUM uses radian as a base unit, so angle quantities are a known non-isomorphism.

questions.text: For this dimension-one quantity, which explicit unit is recorded (one, percent, radian, mole per mole, or another coherent ratio), and is a blank unit forbidden by policy?
If a parts-per-N or percent notation is used, is it a mass ratio, volume ratio or amount-of-substance ratio, and has a deprecated ppb or ppt token been replaced by a power of ten?
Is plane or solid angle being treated as SI dimension one or as a UCUM independent dimension, and which convention must receivers use for commensurability tests?

data_elements.name: Explicit dimensionless unit
data_elements.description: Unit used instead of a blank, such as 1, %, rad or mol/mol.

data_elements.name: Fraction basis
data_elements.description: mass, volume, amount-of-substance, or unspecified, for percent and parts-per notations.

data_elements.name: Angle dimension convention
data_elements.description: si-dimension-one or ucum-independent-radian.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Dimensionless-unit policy is expressed as codes and flags on the quantity value and kind.

bundles.name: Conversion, commensurability and quantity calculus
bundles.description: When two units mean the same thing, when they are merely commensurable, how conversion factors and offsets are applied, and how products and quotients of quantities stay dimensionally homogeneous.
bundles.rationale: UCUM, QUDT and ISO 80000 specify the algebra that agents must run before adding, comparing or converting values. Affine offsets and kind mismatches are the main operational failure modes.

layers.name: Commensurability and conversion
layers.description: Equality versus commensurability of unit expressions, and conversion by multiplier and offset.

findings.name: Unit equality versus commensurability
findings.description: UCUM defines two equivalence relations: equality of units and commensurability of units. Equal expressions denote the same unit; commensurable expressions share a dimension and differ only by magnitude. Full UCUM conformance requires semantic comparison, not string equality, because many expressions denote the same unit. Limited conformance may compare literals. Arbitrary units are commensurable with nothing. Kind mismatches such as gray versus sievert remain incommensurable as quantities even when dimensions match.

questions.text: Do two unit expressions denote the same unit under the governing semantics, even if their literal codes differ?
Are the two units commensurable, and if so what is the relative magnitude of the first regarding the second?
Is the engine operating in full semantic conformance or limited literal conformance, and which expressions will therefore be missed as equivalents?
Does a quantity-kind mismatch block conversion even though the dimension vectors match?

data_elements.name: Semantically equal
data_elements.description: True when two unit expressions map to the same UCUM or QUDT unit.

data_elements.name: Are commensurable
data_elements.description: True when the units share a dimension and a conversion factor exists.

data_elements.name: Relative magnitude
data_elements.description: Scalar r such that u/v = r × 1 for commensurable units.

data_elements.name: UCUM conformance mode
data_elements.description: full or limited, as defined by UCUM section 2.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Equality and commensurability are computed results. They may be cached inline; the algorithm lives in the conversion function.

findings.name: Conversion multiplier and offset
findings.description: QUDT models conversion to a reference unit with a multiplier and an offset so that affine conversions such as Fahrenheit and Celsius are expressible. Linear conversions use offset zero. NIST SP 811 Appendix B tabulates factors from mainly non-SI units into SI and discusses rounding of converted numerical values. Conversion factors themselves have provenance: some are exact by definition after the 2019 SI, others are CODATA experimental values that must be versioned. Original recorded values should be retained because conversion can lose lexical precision.

questions.text: What conversion multiplier and offset map this unit to the named reference unit, and is the mapping exact or experimental?
Which authority, publication and version supplied the conversion factor, and at what observation time was that factor ingested?
What canonical or reporting unit does Dimension policy require, and must the original unit and original numerical value be stored alongside the converted value?
After conversion, how many significant digits are kept, and was rounding applied in the direction required by the receiving process?

data_elements.name: Conversion multiplier
data_elements.description: Factor that multiplies a value in this unit to obtain a value in the reference unit before adding any offset.

data_elements.name: Conversion offset
data_elements.description: Affine offset applied after scaling, zero for linear conversions.

data_elements.name: Is exact conversion
data_elements.description: True when the factor is exact by definition rather than an experimental constant.

data_elements.name: Canonical unit
data_elements.description: Unit chosen by policy for comparison and storage canonicalisation.

artifacts.name: Conversion factor table
artifacts.description: Versioned table of multipliers, offsets, exactness flags and source citations for unit pairs used by the Dimension.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Table version IRI plus each row's from-unit and to-unit pair.

layers.name: Quantity calculus and delta quantities
layers.description: Products, quotients and sums of quantities, and the special case of interval quantities.

findings.name: Quantity calculus and dimensional homogeneity
findings.description: ISO 80000-1 describes quantity calculus: only quantities of the same kind, and therefore the same dimension, may be added or subtracted. Products and quotients produce derived kinds whose dimensions are the corresponding products of powers. Numerical-value equations have the same form as quantity equations only in a coherent system. UCUM implements the algebra as an Abelian group under multiplication with integer exponents. Implementations must refuse mixed-kind addition even when a naive dimension check would pass.

questions.text: What algebraic operation is requested among which operand quantities, and is each operand dimensionally legal for that operation?
What quantity kind, dimension and coherent unit does the result have, and must the numerical value be recomputed in a coherent system to avoid hidden factors?
If a non-coherent unit such as hour or millimetre appears in a product, how are prefix and conversion factors accumulated so that the numerical-value equation stays correct?

data_elements.name: Algebraic operation
data_elements.description: multiply, divide, exponentiate, add or subtract.

data_elements.name: Dimensional homogeneity satisfied
data_elements.description: True when the operands are legal for the operation.

data_elements.name: Accumulated magnitude factor
data_elements.description: Product of non-coherent numeric factors that must be applied to numerical values.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Calculus inputs and outputs are quantity values. Proof of homogeneity is an inline validation result.

findings.name: Delta versus absolute quantity
findings.description: QUDT isDeltaQuantity marks a measure of a change rather than an absolute level, which changes conversion because offsets must not be applied. NIST SP 811 states that a temperature difference may be expressed in kelvin or degree Celsius with equal magnitude. Failure to flag deltas is a common source of 273.15-scale errors. The same pattern applies to other affine scales.

questions.text: Is this quantity a delta or interval rather than an absolute level of the same kind?
Which conversion rule applies: linear multiplier only, or affine multiplier-plus-offset?
If both a level and a delta of the same property exist, how are they related, and may they share a unit symbol that differs only by interpretation?

data_elements.name: Conversion rule
data_elements.description: linear or affine, determined by the delta flag and scale type.

data_elements.name: Offset suppressed
data_elements.description: True when an affine offset must not be applied.

data_elements.name: Related absolute quantity
data_elements.description: Reference to the corresponding absolute-level quantity when both are recorded.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Delta versus absolute is a boolean interpretation flag on the quantity value.

bundles.name: Uncertainty, quality and metrological traceability
bundles.description: How the quality of a quantity value is expressed as measurement uncertainty and how the unit and value are traced to international references.
bundles.rationale: A quantity value used for decision making is incomplete without uncertainty and traceability when the host is a measurement result. GUM and VIM supply the vocabulary; this mixin stores the expressed result, not the full statistical design.

layers.name: Uncertainty expression
layers.description: Standard, combined and expanded uncertainty attached to a quantity value.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty expression
findings.description: GUM establishes general rules for evaluating and expressing uncertainty intended for a broad spectrum of measurements. The standard uncertainty u is a standard deviation. Combined standard uncertainty u_c is obtained from a measurement model relating input quantities to the measurand. Expanded uncertainty U = k × u_c is reported with a coverage factor k and an intended coverage probability. Type A evaluation uses statistical analysis of observations; Type B uses other information. Uncertainty has the same dimension as the measurand and must use a commensurable unit. This mixin records the expressed uncertainty, not the full uncertainty budget process.

questions.text: What standard, combined and expanded uncertainties are attached to this quantity value, in which unit, and with which coverage factor and coverage probability?
Was the uncertainty obtained by Type A statistical evaluation, Type B evaluation, or a combination, and which measurement model version was used?
If uncertainty is absent, is that because the value is a specified requirement rather than a measurement, or is it a quality gap that blocks a decision?
If this quantity is an input to a derived quantity, how must its uncertainty be propagated, and are input quantities correlated?

data_elements.name: Standard uncertainty
data_elements.description: Standard uncertainty u of the quantity value.

data_elements.name: Expanded uncertainty
data_elements.description: Expanded uncertainty U = k × u_c.

data_elements.name: Coverage factor
data_elements.description: Coverage factor k used to obtain U from u_c.

data_elements.name: Coverage probability
data_elements.description: Intended coverage probability associated with U, typically 0.95.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty evaluation type
data_elements.description: A, B, or combined, as defined by GUM.

artifacts.name: Uncertainty statement
artifacts.description: Optional serialised statement of u, u_c, U, k, coverage probability and evaluation type bound to a quantity value.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Host measurement identifier plus statement version; UUID if the Dimension freezes the statement independently.

layers.name: Traceability and evidence
layers.description: Traceability of units and values to international metrological standards, and evidence retained for that claim.

findings.name: Metrological traceability and evidence
findings.description: VIM defines metrological traceability as a property of a measurement result whereby the result can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty. ISO 11240 requires units used in medicinal-product interchange to be traceable to international metrological standards and provides mapping structures among vocabularies. After 20 May 2019 the SI reference is the set of defining constants rather than artefacts such as the international prototype of the kilogram. Claims of traceability without a chain are not conformance.

questions.text: To which international reference is this quantity value or unit claimed to be traceable, and is the calibration chain documented end to end?
What evidence artefacts support the traceability claim, such as a calibration certificate identifier, mise en pratique citation, or mapping table version?
Which organisation is responsible for maintaining the traceability claim, and under which accreditation or metrological authority?
Where does the chain stop, and is the result therefore only internally consistent rather than metrologically traceable?

data_elements.name: Traceability reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an SI defining constant, a national standard, or another stated metrological reference.

data_elements.name: Calibration chain documented
data_elements.description: True when an unbroken documented chain exists.

data_elements.name: Calibration certificate identifier
data_elements.description: Master identifier of a calibration certificate when one exists. Digital calibration certificate formats are an evidence gap if not supplied.

data_elements.name: Responsible organisation
data_elements.description: Organisation accountable for the traceability statement.

artifacts.name: Traceability record
artifacts.description: Documented chain from the quantity value or unit to a stated international reference, including certificate identifiers and mapping versions.
media_or_form: XML DCC if provided by host
artifacts.identity_strategy: Certificate or chain master identifier from the issuing metrology body; Dimension UUID only as a local surrogate.

bundles.name: Coding, mapping and interoperability
bundles.description: Machine codes and IRIs for units, and the mappings and conflicts among UCUM, UNECE Recommendation 20, QUDT, SI/ISO 80000 and health-informatics IDMP units.
bundles.rationale: Agents interchange quantities across trade, health, science and engineering. Primary vocabularies overlap but are not equivalent; mappings are alignments, not silent conformance.

layers.name: Unit code systems
layers.description: The principal public code systems and semantic vocabularies for units.

findings.name: Compositional unit codes (UCUM)
findings.description: UCUM is a grammar that generates infinitely many valid expressions from a closed table of atoms and prefixes using multiplication, division, integer exponents, parentheses and annotations. It is intended for unambiguous electronic communication rather than typographic print. Case-sensitive and case-insensitive variants are incompatible. Whitespace is not a separator and may be treated as an error. ISO 11240 and FHIR recommend UCUM for machine-readable units. Full name and print symbol are out of UCUM scope.

questions.text: Is the unit expression a valid UCUM main-term under the published grammar, and is it case-sensitive or case-insensitive?
What annotation, if any, is present in curly braces, and has it been stripped before semantic comparison?
Which UCUM version and which terminal-symbol table revision define this expression, and would a later prefix or atom change the parse?

data_elements.name: UCUM expression
data_elements.description: Full UCUM main-term, not only an atom.

data_elements.name: Case variant
data_elements.description: cs or ci as defined by UCUM.

data_elements.name: UCUM version
data_elements.description: Specification version such as 2.2 dated 2024-06-17.

artifacts.name: UCUM specification snapshot
artifacts.description: Versioned snapshot of the UCUM grammar and terminal-symbol tables used by the Dimension.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Specification URL plus version and date 2024-06-17 or later adopted revision.

findings.name: Tabulated trade codes (UNECE Rec 20)
findings.description: UN/ECE Recommendation 20 provides three-character alphabetic and alphanumeric codes for units of measure used in international trade, listed by quantity category and intended for manual and automated exchange among trade participants. Codes are tabulated, not compositional: there is no grammar for arbitrary products of units. QUDT exposes uneceCommonCode as a crosswalk property. Rec 20 codes are therefore complements to UCUM, not substitutes, and a Dimension that speaks both EDI and clinical or scientific messages must map rather than assume identity.

questions.text: What UNECE Recommendation 20 common code identifies this unit in trade messages, and in which quantity category annex is it listed?
What UCUM expression, if any, is the declared equivalent of this Rec 20 code, and is the mapping one-to-one or many-to-one?
Which revision of the Recommendation 20 code list is in force for this message, and has the code been added, renamed or withdrawn?

data_elements.name: Rec 20 quantity category
data_elements.description: Annex category such as length, area, volume/capacity, mass, time or other.

data_elements.name: Rec 20 revision
data_elements.description: Code-list revision identifier used in the interchange.

data_elements.name: Trade code status
data_elements.description: active, added, renamed or withdrawn.

artifacts.name: UNECE Recommendation 20 code list
artifacts.description: The three annexes of Rec 20 unit codes adopted by the Dimension, with revision identity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: UNECE recommendation and revision identifier; codes are the row keys.

findings.name: Semantic unit IRIs (QUDT)
findings.description: QUDT assigns IRIs to units, quantity kinds, dimension vectors and systems, and records conversionMultiplier, conversionOffset, ucumCode, uneceCommonCode, iec61360Code and omUnit links. It is the preferred governed global identifier layer when a Dimension needs RDF-stable identity independent of any one encoding grammar. QUDT also includes CurrencyUnit, which this mixin must not treat as an SI quantity. Schema 2.1.29 is dated 2023-07-28; later vocabulary graphs may add units without changing the schema.

questions.text: What QUDT unit IRI and quantity-kind IRI identify this concept, and which vocabulary graph version was used?
Which UCUM, UNECE, IEC 61360 and OM identifiers does the QUDT resource assert, and are any of those assertions missing or conflicting?
Is the QUDT resource a CurrencyUnit or otherwise out of this mixin's physical-quantity scope?

data_elements.name: QUDT unit IRI
data_elements.description: IRI under http://qudt.org/vocab/unit or the adopted graph.

data_elements.name: QUDT graph version
data_elements.description: Schema or vocabulary release identifier.

data_elements.name: Is currency unit
data_elements.description: True when the QUDT type is CurrencyUnit and the concept is out of scope of this mixin.

artifacts.name: QUDT vocabulary snapshot
artifacts.description: Adopted snapshot of QUDT unit and quantity-kind graphs used for IRI identity.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Graph IRI plus catalog modified date.

layers.name: Mapping and conflicts
layers.description: Crosswalks among vocabularies and recorded conflicts that block silent conformance claims.

findings.name: Crosswalks and recorded conflicts
findings.description: ISO 11240 defines structures and rules for mapping among unit vocabularies and language translations because existing dictionaries use different terms and codes. Known primary conflicts include: UCUM's defining basis is not isomorphic with the SI; UCUM 2.2 prefixes may lag the 2022 SI prefix additions; NIST SP 811 remains on pre-2019 base-unit definitions; gray, sievert, becquerel and hertz share dimensions with different kinds; energy in joule and torque in newton metre share dimension; litre has both l and L case-sensitive codes; billion-based parts-per tokens are deprecated in UCUM; Rec 20 tabulated codes cannot express arbitrary UCUM products; FHIR Money is separate from Quantity. Alignments must record these rather than claim universal conformance.

questions.text: Which source vocabulary concept is mapped to which target vocabulary concept, with what mapping type (equivalent, broader, incommensurable, kind-mismatch)?
What conflict or non-isomorphism applies to this pair, and is automatic conversion therefore refused?
What language-specific unit names are bound to this concept, and which language is authoritative for print?
Who authorised this mapping, under which ISO 11240 or Dimension rule, and at what version?

data_elements.name: Mapping type
data_elements.description: equivalent, broader, narrower, incommensurable, kind-mismatch, or unmatched.

data_elements.name: Conflict code
data_elements.description: Identifier of a recorded conflict such as ucum-si-non-isomorphic or prefix-set-lag.

data_elements.name: Automatic conversion refused
data_elements.description: True when the mapping forbids silent conversion.

data_elements.name: Mapping version
data_elements.description: Version identity of the crosswalk table.

artifacts.name: Unit vocabulary crosswalk
artifacts.description: Authorised mappings among UCUM, Rec 20, QUDT, SI names and local codes, with conflict flags.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Crosswalk table IRI plus version; row identity is source-system, source-code, target-system, target-code.

bundles.name: Governance, policy and lifecycle
bundles.description: Authority, allowed-unit policy, provenance, retention of original values, access, and the AGENTS.md bootstrap contract for operating this mixin.
bundles.rationale: As an embeddable value object the mixin still needs Dimension-level governance: who may define units, which units may be used, how originals are kept, and how an agent discovers specification, storage, interface and process URLs.

layers.name: Authority, ownership and lifecycle
layers.description: Who defines units and conversion factors, and how those definitions version, deprecate and take effect.

findings.name: Unit authority and versioning
findings.description: The SI is defined by the SI Brochure published by the BIPM under CGPM resolutions; the 26th CGPM (2018) redefinition took effect on 20 May 2019. UCUM terminal tables may change only by approved revision. ISO 80000-1:2022 supersedes the 2009 edition. QUDT schema and vocabulary graphs version independently. A Dimension must record which of these authorities it treats as master for each unit class, the effective time of a definition, and the ingestion time of that definition into the Dimension. Deprecation is the allowed terminal state; physical deletion of a published unit definition is not.

questions.text: Which organisation is the master authority for this unit or conversion factor, and which specification URL and version are in force?
What is the effective event time of this definition in the world, and what is the observation or ingestion time into this Dimension?
Is the unit or mapping active, deprecated, withdrawn, or superseded, and what identifier replaces it?
Who is the Dimension owner or maintainer accountable for adopting this definition, and who may approve local aliases?

data_elements.name: Master authority
data_elements.description: Organisation that defines the unit or factor, such as BIPM, UCUM Organization, ISO or UNECE.

data_elements.name: Specification URL
data_elements.description: Canonical HTTPS URL of the in-force specification.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: active, deprecated, withdrawn or superseded.

data_elements.name: Effective from
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time at which the definition became true in the world, for example 2019-05-20T00:00:00Z for the revised SI.

data_elements.name: Ingested at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time at which the Dimension ingested the definition, distinct from effective-from.

artifacts.name: Authority adoption record
artifacts.description: Dimension decision record naming the master authorities, specification versions and effective times for unit definitions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dimension decision identifier; not a date.

layers.name: Allowed units and constraints
layers.description: Policy that restricts which units, prefixes and code systems may appear in a context of use.

findings.name: Allowed units policy
findings.description: Context of use frequently restricts units: laboratory observations may bind UCUM, trade messages may bind Rec 20, scientific reporting may require SI coherent units. NIST SP 811 provides a manuscript checklist for SI usage. ISO 11240 limits itself to computer interchange of medicinal-product units and requires traceability. Dimension policy must state required code systems, forbidden customary units, whether unit one may be blank, whether currency may appear, and what happens when an inbound unit is unknown.

questions.text: Which unit codes and systems are allowed, preferred or forbidden in this context of use?
If an inbound unit is unknown or unmapped, is the value rejected, stored as free text without conversion, or queued for stewardship?
Does this context require SI units, SI-accepted units, or permit customary units with mandatory dual reporting?
Who may read versus change the allowed-units policy, and which audit events are required when the list changes?

data_elements.name: Required coding system URI
data_elements.description: Unit system required in this context, such as http://unitsofmeasure.org.

data_elements.name: SI usage policy
data_elements.description: si-only, si-and-accepted, or customary-permitted.

data_elements.name: Unknown unit action
data_elements.description: reject, store-text, or queue-for-steward.

data_elements.name: Dual reporting required
data_elements.description: True when a customary unit must be accompanied by an SI equivalent.

artifacts.name: Allowed units policy
artifacts.description: Serialised policy listing allowed, preferred and forbidden units and systems for named contexts of use.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Policy identifier plus version; context-of-use code as a key, not a date.

layers.name: Retention, access and agent bootstrap
layers.description: How original values are retained, who may see conversion tables versus raw values, and the mandatory AGENTS.md contract.

findings.name: Original value retention, deletion and access
findings.description: Converted numerical values can lose lexical precision and depend on a versioned factor. The original unit, original lexical decimal, conversion table version and conversion time must be retained for as long as the host record is retained. Unit definitions are deprecated rather than deleted so that historical values remain interpretable. Access control applies to bundles, layers, findings and artefacts: conversion-factor tables and uncertainty statements may be more sensitive than a public SI symbol list. Quantity values inherit host-record access unless a Dimension assigns a tighter scope.

questions.text: What original numerical value, original unit, conversion version and conversion time must be retained, and for how long relative to the host record?
Under what conditions may a quantity value be deleted or redacted, and is the unit definition itself never deleted, only deprecated?
Which access scope applies to this quantity value, conversion table or uncertainty statement, and what exception allows an agent to read conversion factors without reading host personal data?
What audit record is written when a value is converted, a factor table is patched, or an original value is redacted?

data_elements.name: Original numerical value
data_elements.description: Lexical numerical value as first recorded, before conversion.

data_elements.name: Original unit code
data_elements.description: Unit in which the value was first recorded.

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration or policy code for retaining original and converted values.

data_elements.name: Unit definition indelible
data_elements.description: True when published unit definitions may be deprecated but not physically deleted.

data_elements.name: Access scope
data_elements.description: bundle, layer, finding or artefact scope that governs this record.

artifacts.name: Original quantity value snapshot
artifacts.description: Frozen copy of the originally recorded lexical value, unit, system, comparator and conversion provenance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Host record master identifier plus snapshot UUID assigned by the Dimension; event time is not the identifier.

findings.name: AGENTS.md bootstrap contract
findings.description: Every adopting Dimension must publish an AGENTS.md that names the model and points agents to specification, storage type, interface and process URLs, independent of whether the projection is files, MongoDB, MCP or another interface. JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git and MongoDB remain projections of this mixin, not its semantics.

questions.text: Does AGENTS.md declare Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL for WM-XCT-008?
In what order must an agent read AGENTS.md, the specification, the allowed-units policy and the conversion table before writing a quantity value?
Which storage type and interface project this mixin, and are agents forbidden from treating that projection as the semantic model?

data_elements.name: AGENTS.md Name
data_elements.description: Declared name of the governed model, Quantity / Unit.

data_elements.name: AGENTS.md Type
data_elements.description: Declared type, mixin, matching entry_kind.

data_elements.name: Storage type URL
data_elements.description: URL documenting the storage projection, which is not the mixin semantics.

data_elements.name: Interface URL
data_elements.description: URL of the access interface, such as an API or MCP endpoint description.

data_elements.name: Processes URL
data_elements.description: URL of operating processes for validation, conversion and stewardship.

artifacts.name: AGENTS.md
artifacts.description: Mandatory bootstrap file for agents operating WM-XCT-008, independent of storage projection.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Fixed filename AGENTS.md at the Dimension root for this model; content identifies Name, Type and the four URLs.

functions.name: Canonicalize unit expression
functions.description: Parse a unit expression in the governing grammar, strip semantically empty annotations, and return a semantic canonical form for equality comparison.
preconditions: A grammar version has been adopted.
The expression uses the declared case variant.
effects: Does not alter the originally recorded expression.
Produces a canonical form usable by equality and conversion functions.

functions.name: Test commensurability
functions.description: Decide whether two quantity values or units share a dimension and compatible quantity kinds so that comparison or conversion is legal.
preconditions: Both sides have a resolvable unit or dimension.
Arbitrary units are treated as incommensurable with everything.
effects: Refuses conversion when kinds share a dimension but are not comparable, such as gray versus sievert.

functions.name: Convert quantity value
functions.description: Convert a numerical value from a source unit to a target unit using multiplier and offset, suppressing offset when the quantity is a delta.
preconditions: A conversion row exists for the unit pair and table version.
Special units supply forward or inverse functions when required.
effects: Leaves the original value, unit and lexical decimal unchanged.
Records conversion table version and conversion time.

functions.name: Apply quantity calculus
functions.description: Multiply, divide, exponentiate, add or subtract quantity values under dimensional homogeneity and coherent-factor accounting.
preconditions: Addition and subtraction require same kind, not only same dimension.
Operands are not arbitrary units unless the operation is explicitly local to that assay.

functions.name: Validate quantity binding
functions.description: Check that a quantity value satisfies coding invariants, allowed-units policy, scale constraints and explicit unit-one rules.
preconditions: If a unit code is present, a unit system URI is present.
effects: May reject, accept, or route an unknown unit to stewardship without converting it.

functions.name: Map unit code
functions.description: Translate a unit identifier from one vocabulary to another using an authorised crosswalk, recording mapping type and conflicts.
preconditions: Currency codes are not mapped into SI units.
effects: Returns unmatched rather than inventing an equivalent.
Surfaces recorded non-isomorphisms such as UCUM versus SI angle.

functions.name: Attach uncertainty statement
functions.description: Bind a GUM-style uncertainty expression to a quantity value, requiring a commensurable uncertainty unit.
outputs: validation errors if units differ in dimension
preconditions: The host role is a measured result rather than a pure specification, or policy allows specified tolerances.
Uncertainty unit is commensurable with the value unit.
effects: Does not compute Type A statistics; it records an already evaluated statement.
Marks missing uncertainty as a quality gap when policy requires it.

functions.name: Freeze original quantity value
functions.description: Create an immutable snapshot of the originally recorded lexical value, unit, comparator and provenance before any conversion.
preconditions: A host master identifier exists or the Dimension assigns a UUID.
Event time and ingestion time are recorded separately when known.
effects: Makes the original lexical form indelible for the host retention period.
Subsequent conversions reference the snapshot rather than overwriting it.

composition.purpose: Embed quantity value, unit, kind, dimension and uncertainty into a host measurement or observation that owns procedure, instrument, subject, place and time.

composition.target: SI Brochure / International System of Units
composition.purpose: Align physical units, prefixes, defining constants and dimension-one guidance with the SI without claiming that every stored unit is an SI unit.
Align quantity calculus, symbols and the quantity = numerical value × unit equation with ISO 80000-1.
Use UCUM as the preferred compositional machine grammar while recording that its basis is not isomorphic with the SI.
Use QUDT IRIs and conversion properties as governed global identifiers and semantic crosswalks.
Reference tabulated trade unit codes when the host message is international trade EDI rather than a compositional scientific expression.
Align coded-unit interchange, vocabulary mapping and traceability requirements used in medicinal-product identification.
Exclude currency amounts from this mixin and point to a sibling money model; FHIR Money and QUDT CurrencyUnit remain out of scope.
Keep duration quantities in this mixin while leaving instants, time zones and civil calendars to a time model.
Prevent packaging counts such as tablet or vial from being treated as metrological units.
Keep length, area, volume and angle as quantities while leaving CRS, geodesy and pixels to a spatial model.
Extend quantity values with VIM vocabulary and optional GUM uncertainty statements without absorbing the full metrology process model.

owner_package_requirements: Designate a Quantity/Unit steward accountable for adopting SI, UCUM, Rec 20 and QUDT versions and for approving local aliases.
Publish an allowed-units policy per context of use, including required coding systems, SI policy, unknown-unit action and dual-reporting rules.
Version conversion-factor tables separately from quantity values, with exactness flags and ingestion timestamps.
Prohibit physical deletion of published unit definitions; allow deprecation and replacement identifiers only.
Keep original lexical values and units for the host retention period whenever conversion is performed.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-owned IRI namespace for local unit aliases and quantity-kind overlays, for example under the adopting Dimension's NAV.XCT.QTY path, and prefer BIPM/SI names, QUDT IRIs or UCUM codes as the first-class identifiers rather than inventing parallel codes. Do not treat file paths, MongoDB collection names or MCP tool names as namespace semantics.
registry_links: vr.wm-xct-008 Quantity / Unit mixin in the world-model registry

canonicalization_rules: Canonical comparison of physical units uses UCUM semantic equality when a UCUM code exists; otherwise QUDT IRI equality; otherwise Dimension UUID. Literal string equality is limited conformance only.
Quantity values presented for comparison are converted to a policy canonical unit without overwriting the original lexical decimal.
Dimension vectors used for homogeneity checks are expressed in a named basis; UCUM and SI bases must not be silently mixed.
Trailing zeros in lexical decimals are preserved for presentation precision even if calculation uses a binary float internally.
Annotations in UCUM curly braces are stripped before canonical comparison.
patch_rules: Published unit definitions are patched only by adding a new versioned record with effective-from and replaced-by, never by rewriting history.
Conversion-factor patches must cite authority, version and ingested-at, and must recompute derived values rather than edit frozen originals.
Quantity value patches on a host record version the host; the frozen original snapshot remains immutable.
Allowed-units policy patches are audited and take effect only from an explicit RFC 3339 effective-from.
compatibility_rules: A receiver in limited UCUM conformance may fail to recognise semantic equivalents; senders that require interoperation SHOULD also emit a canonical UCUM expression.
Alignment with SI, ISO 80000, UCUM, QUDT, Rec 20 or FHIR is not a conformance claim unless the Dimension records evidence against a named version.
2019 SI defining constants supersede artefact-based kilogram language in NIST SP 811 Appendix A for any new work.
Binary information prefixes must not be treated as SI prefixes.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier from BIPM, ISO, UCUM, UNECE or QUDT for the unit or vocabulary artefact.
Governed global identifier or IRI adopted by the Dimension, including QUDT unit IRIs and specification DOIs.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension for original-value snapshots, policy records and local aliases when no master identifier exists.
A date, effective-from timestamp or brochure edition year is metadata, not an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All event times and observation or ingestion times use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; record event time and observation/ingestion time separately when both are known.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artefacts use a stable kebab-case stem, a version or serial number, and a master identifier in the name or header, for example unit-crosswalk-v3.json or si-prefix-table-2022; timestamps may appear as metadata fields but must not be the sole identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Serial artefacts carry a cryptographic hash of the canonical bytes and a provenance citation to the source URL and version_or_date; conversion tables additionally record whether each factor is exact.

policies: Unknown or unmapped inbound units are not converted; they follow the Dimension unknown-unit action of reject, store-text or queue-for-steward.
Original recorded quantity values are retained at least as long as the host record and are not overwritten by canonicalised forms.
Unit definitions are deprecated, not deleted, so historical values remain interpretable.
Currency, calendar instants, geometry and units of presentation are out of scope and must be refused or redirected to sibling models.
Uncertainty, when required by the host measurement context, uses GUM terms and a unit commensurable with the value.

read: Any agent with scope on the host record may read embedded quantity values at the finding level.
Conversion-factor tables and allowed-units policies are readable by conversion agents without granting host personal-data access.
create: Quantity values are created only as embeds on a host record by a data producer role, with unit binding validated against policy.
New local unit aliases require steward approval and a mapping to a master identifier.
Original-value snapshots are created automatically before conversion.
update: Host quantity values may be corrected by a new host version; frozen snapshots are not updated.
Unit definitions and conversion tables are updated only by appending a versioned record with effective-from.
Comparator, kind or delta flags may be corrected when evidence shows they were misclassified, with audit.
delete: Embedded quantity values are deleted only under the host record's retention and redaction policy.
Unit vocabulary entries are not physically deleted.
Conversion derived values may be dropped if the original snapshot remains.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Accountable for adopting this mixin, publishing AGENTS.md, and naming master authorities and namespaces.

roles.name: Quantity and unit steward
responsibilities: Maintain allowed-units policy, local aliases, crosswalks and prefix-table versions, and resolve unknown-unit queues.

roles.name: Metrology steward
responsibilities: Decide SI policy, traceability claims, uncertainty requirements and treatment of special, arbitrary and delta quantities.

roles.name: Quantity data producer
responsibilities: Record original lexical values, units, kinds, comparators and event times on host records without premature conversion.

roles.name: Conversion agent
responsibilities: Run canonicalisation, commensurability tests and conversions using the in-force factor table, retaining originals.

roles.name: Auditor
responsibilities: Inspect conversion provenance, access exceptions, deprecation decisions and retention of original-value snapshots.

access.default_rule: Quantity values inherit the host record's access control; unit vocabularies, prefix tables and SI symbol lists are readable by operating agents; conversion-factor patches and uncertainty statements follow the tighter of host access and finding-level restriction.
exceptions: A conversion agent may read conversion-factor tables and unit vocabularies without access to host personal data.
Redacted original values remain visible to auditors for the retention period even when producers can no longer read them.
audit_requirements: Record actor, event time, ingestion time, artefact identity and before/after version for conversion, policy change, deprecation and redaction.
Audit unknown-unit exceptions and refused conversions caused by kind mismatch or missing mapping.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md for Name, Type and the four URLs.
Read the specification at Specification URL for quantity, unit, dimension and uncertainty semantics.
Read the allowed-units policy and conversion table identified from Processes URL before writing or converting any quantity value.
Treat Storage type URL and Interface URL as projections, not as the mixin semantics.

coverage.claim: This mixin captures the defensible operating surface of quantity kinds, dimensions, units, quantity values, conversion, coded vocabularies and GUM-style uncertainty for an embeddable Quantity/Unit context, grounded in BIPM SI, VIM, GUM, ISO 80000-1, UCUM, QUDT, FHIR Quantity, UNECE Rec 20, NIST SP 811 and ISO 11240. It does not claim a universal ontology of all measurable properties or legal-metrology completeness.

checklist.notes: Unit identity priority is master IRI or code, then governed global identifier, then Dimension UUID; quantity values as embeds are optionally identified only when frozen.
Active, deprecated, withdrawn and superseded states for units and mappings; SI 2019 effective time; unit definitions are not physically deleted.
Kind-to-unit applicability, host embedding, same-dimension peer kinds, mapping pairs, and sibling exclusions for money, time, geometry and presentation units.
Event time versus observation/ingestion time on values and on definition adoption; RFC 3339 required; duration units in scope, instants out of scope.
Conversion-factor authority and version, traceability chain, original-value snapshots, and audit of conversion and policy change.
Dimension owner, quantity/unit steward, metrology steward and responsible organisation for traceability claims.
UCUM parse, qty-3 system-with-code, dimensional homogeneity, allowed-units policy, kind mismatch and special-unit offset rules.
Default inherit-from-host with bundle, layer, finding and artefact scopes, plus conversion-table exception and auditor exception.
Original lexical values retained with the host; unit definitions indelible except by deprecation; redaction under host policy.
UCUM, Rec 20, QUDT, SI/ISO 80000, FHIR Quantity and ISO 11240 alignments with recorded non-isomorphisms.
ISQ/SI kinds, QUDT QuantityKind, dimension vectors, dimension one and angle convention conflict.
Equality versus commensurability, multiplier and offset, delta versus absolute, ratio versus interval versus logarithmic scales.
GUM standard, combined and expanded uncertainty, coverage factor and Type A/B evaluation type attached to values.
Location of a measurement belongs to the host or a geometry model; length and angle remain quantities without CRS identity.

known_omissions: Full text of ISO 80000-1:2022 and ISO 11240:2012 is paywalled; abstracts and public tables of contents were used, so clause-level data-element names from those standards may be incomplete.
UCUM 2.2 prefix table as published 2024-06-17 does not show ronna, quetta, ronto or quecto; whether a later UCUM revision added them was not verified beyond this version.
OIML legal-metrology instruments, WELMEC guides and national weights-and-measures statutes were not taken as primary sources.
Digital calibration certificate (DCC) schemas, CODATA least-squares constant adjustments after 2019, and VIM4 draft revisions are not incorporated.
IEC 80000-13 information-science units, UDUNITS, OM ontology, SensorML/SWE Quantity, UN/CEFACT CCTS Quantity.Type and schema.org QuantitativeValue are discovery alignments only.
Vector, tensor, complex, distributional and interval-arithmetic quantity types beyond FHIR Range are not modelled.
Catalytic enzyme units, WHO International Units and other biological potency systems are covered only as arbitrary/procedure-defined units.
conflicts: UCUM defining bases (metre, second, gram, radian, kelvin, coulomb, candela) are not isomorphic with SI bases; mole is a count in UCUM and radian is a base, whereas SI treats the radian as a dimensionless derived unit.
NIST SP 811 Appendix A still states pre-2019 artefact-based base-unit definitions and the publication itself warns it has not been updated for the 2019 SI.
SI Brochure guidance after version 3.01 urges explicit units for quantities of dimension one, which conflicts with widespread practice of omitting the unit one.
Gray versus sievert and joule versus newton metre share dimensions but not quantity kinds; dimension-only converters will silently mis-convert.
UNECE Rec 20 tabulated three-character codes cannot express arbitrary UCUM products, so trade and scientific unit languages are not 1:1.
FHIR treats Money as distinct from Quantity, while QUDT includes CurrencyUnit in the same schema family.
Degree Celsius is an SI unit that is incoherent with the SI in UCUM special-unit semantics; prefixing Celsius scales the numerical value, not a ratio-scale unit.
regional_assumptions: SI is treated as the default physical system of units; US customary and Imperial units are supported only as named non-SI systems with explicit variants such as US versus Imperial gallon.
English and French names in the SI Brochure are both authentic; this research used English texts.
UNECE Rec 20 is assumed for international trade EDI; some jurisdictions mandate additional national unit lists that were not reviewed.
ISO 11240 is global IDMP but operationally driven by medicines regulators; non-health Dimensions may ignore it without losing SI alignment.
NIST SP 811 informs US style and conversion rounding but is not a substitute for the current SI Brochure.
adversarial_checks: If an agent converts gray to sievert or joule to newton metre because the dimension vectors match, the model has failed the kind-mismatch constraint.
If an agent applies a 273.15 offset to a temperature interval marked as a delta, conversion is wrong.
If an agent treats a UCUM curly-brace annotation as a unit, or treats {RBC} as commensurable with 1, semantic comparison is wrong.
If an agent deletes a deprecated unit so that a historical millimetre-of-mercury value can no longer be interpreted, retention policy is violated.
If an agent claims SI conformance while storing UCUM radian as an independent base without recording the non-isomorphism, the alignment has been over-claimed.
If a currency amount is stored as a Quantity with system ISO 4217 instead of being redirected to a money sibling, scope has been breached.
If conversion overwrites the original lexical decimal 0.010 to 0.01, presentation precision required by FHIR decimal has been lost.
